author: BeauHD
description: Rockstar Games' Grand Theft Auto VI generated a record-breaking $3.79 billion in preorders and first-day sales, making it the biggest entertainment launch in history, according to parent company Take-Two Interactive. The figure surpasses the lifetime global box-office earnings of Avengers: Endgame ($2.9 billion) and comes after more than a decade of development at a reported cost of $1.5 billion. The game developer declined to disclose the number of 'GTA 6' copies sold. "It is with immense gratitude that we enter a new chapter of Rockstar Games with the release of 'Grand Theft Auto VI,'" Rockstar Games president and founder Sam Houser said. "We are incredibly humbled by the response from players around the world and we couldn't be more excited to share this moment with you." Further reading: Gamers Skip Work to Play GTA VI After 13-Year Wait
title: GTA 6 Hits Massive $3.79 Billion In First-Day Sales

author: BeauHD
description:
Signal is introducing default-on screenshot restrictions to prevent AI agents from reading private conversations, warning that increasingly powerful assistants integrated into operating systems pose an "existential threat" to its privacy guarantees. "Right now, these agentic AI integrations are changing this environment in a way that's making it increasingly hostile to privacy. This is an existential threat to Signal, and our ability to responsibly uphold our mission," it said in a blog post. Reuters reports: Signal, widely regarded by privacy advocates as a leader in secure messaging, called its new protections "incomplete" and urged operating system providers Apple, Alphabet's Google and Microsoft to give app developers more concrete ways to block the agents from accessing sensitive data. It also called on those companies to provide more information about how their agents function, so developers can assess what data the bots are accessing and adjust their systems accordingly.

title: Signal Restricts Screenshots to Block AI Agents From Reading Messages

author: BeauHD
description:
Longtime Slashdot reader fahrbot-bot shares a report from CNBC: President Donald Trump on Friday said U.S. companies will be banned from building data centers in other countries and will face a "tremendous tax" penalty if they do so. "We're going to fight very hard for the data centers," Trump said at a White House press conference before announcing the new policy -- which apparently came as news to his own staff. "I don't know if that's a breaking story," Trump said. "I haven't even said that to my people. But I'm telling them now they're here."
 
International expansion represents a growth opportunity for the top cloud infrastructure providers, which want to serve clients from data centers that are nearby, sometimes to meet regulatory requirements. Trump said Friday, however, that if companies want to continue building the centers outside the U.S., "they can, but we're going to put a tremendous tax on them." "We have a lot of places that want them badly, and they're great places. Th
title: Trump Vows To Stop US Companies From Building Data Centers Abroad

author: BeauHD
description: U.S. stocks extended their sell-off Friday as Anthropic shares plunged more than 11% on their second day of trading, despite the AI company's record-setting IPO a day earlier. The Nasdaq fell more than 3%, wiping out its gains for 2026, while the S&P 500 dropped nearly 2% and joined the Dow in correction territory, down at least 10% from recent highs. NBC News reports: The S&P 500 was trading nearly 2% lower as it headed for its worst losing week since April 2025, when President Donald Trump announced his "Liberation Day" tariffs, and is now 10% off from its most recent high, entering what's known as "correction territory." Meanwhile, the tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite was off more than 3% and officially erasing all its previous gains in 2026. Other major AI-related names such as CoreWeave, Nvidia and Oracle also sold off. The six consecutive declining S&P 500 sessions mark the index's longest losing streak since April 2024. A seventh losing day would make it the longest stre
title: Anthropic Shares Tank After Huge IPO As the Nasdaq Erases 2026 Gains

author: BeauHD
description: An anonymous reader quotes a report from Ars Technica: TP-Link, which may be the top provider of wireless routers for US homes and small businesses, isn't allowed to sell its latest Wi-Fi routers in the US. The Trump administration imposed a sweeping ban on foreign-made consumer routers in March 2026, and TP-Link hasn't been able to obtain an exemption. The rules prevent the import or sale of all new router models that are manufactured, assembled, designed, or developed outside the US. The Trump administration has control over which router makers receive special permission to import and sell new products through a waiver-review process involving the Federal Communications Commission, the Department of Defense, and the Department of Homeland Security. While some of its competitors have obtained exemptions to the ban, TP-Link appears to be having a hard time making its case to government officials. Its routers approved before the March 2026 ban remain available for sale in the US, but i
title: Trump Admin Still Won't Let TP-Link Sell Routers In US

author: BeauHD
description: California Attorney General Rob Bonta has issued subpoenas to Nvidia and former CEO Jensen Huang regarding reports that they misled investors about advanced AI chips potentially reaching China. "The conduct of Nvidia and its former CEO raises bright red flags, including about the ways in which the company may have misled investors," Bonta said in a press release. "My office is investigating whether Nvidia or Jensen Huang's actions resulted in China obtaining advanced chips or confidential information -- and if Nvidia misled investors and the public about this risk, in violation of the law." The probe follows Huang's resignation amid allegations involving a suspected Chinese spy and comes as the SEC reportedly conducts a similar investigation. The Hill reports: Bonta's office said the information obtained through the subpoenas will help it to determine if Nvidia, which is based in Santa Clara, Calif., violated state law through its alleged actions. "Nvidia is in a messy, transnational
title: California Issues Subpoena to Nvidia Over Chip Sales to China

author: BeauHD
description:
President Trump has named Pentagon Chief Information Officer Kirsten A. Davies as his new national cyber director, replacing Sean Cairncross amid a broader shakeup of the administration's cybersecurity and AI leadership. According to Axios, White House Chief of Staff Stephen Miller pushed for Cairncross' removal over concerns about his technical qualifications. From the report: "Kirsten has the credentials to excel in this position and has already been Senate-confirmed," an administration official said. At the Pentagon, Davies has been the top adviser to Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth "on all matters relating to information management, information technology, cybersecurity, and information assurance," according to her bio.
 
Before serving in the Trump administration, Davies worked for Unilever and "led global cyber resilience for one of the world's largest consumer goods enterprises," her bio says. Davies' career also has included technology and cyber roles at Estee Lauder, Barclays-
title: White House Replaces Cyber Director After Tech Outages

author: BeauHD
description: Google is rolling out a redesigned desktop homepage that adds a collapsible sidebar for accessing and continuing previous AI Mode searches. Google's vice president of product, Robby Stein, says the company is rolling out the option because "people are coming to Search with more questions that aren't just one and done," adding that "in testing, this sidebar made a big difference for making progress & continuing to explore the web." The Verge reports: It's yet another big change for Google's homepage, which has long presented you with a single bar to kick off your web search. The company brought its AI Mode button to its search bar last year, which opens up a chatbot-like search experience within Google. In May, Google updated its search box to accommodate longer queries and added AI-powered autocomplete.
title: Google Is Putting AI Chats Right On the Homepage

author: BeauHD
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from TechCrunch: The U.K. government has been ordered to confirm that it issued a secret order demanding Apple to provide authorities with encrypted customer information. The Thursday ruling from the U.K.'s Investigatory Powers Tribunal, an independent court that allows citizens to challenge government surveillance orders, is a rare rebuke for the government, which sought to keep the encryption backdoor order a state secret. The tribunal's ruling rejected the Home Office's claim that disclosing the order would be damaging to national security. [...] A final hearing on what specific order details can be released is anticipated next year. The order follows a year-long dispute that began when British authorities reportedly sought a backdoor to users' data worldwide, drawing criticism from U.S. lawmakers over privacy concerns. Rather than comply, Apple disabled its Advanced Data Protection feature for U.K. users and challenged the order in court.
 
The
title: UK Government Forced To Disclose Secret Apple Backdoor Order

author: BeauHD
description: Intuit has agreed to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for $3.68 billion in cash and stock, less than one-third of the $12 billion it paid to acquire the email-marketing platform in 2021. The deal is set to close in early 2027. CNBC reports: In August Intuit started running Mailchimp as a distinct operating segment. The move was meant to give investors more transparency as the company tried to manage the unit for profitability, Sandeep Aujla, Intuit's finance chief, said at a September company briefing. Also on Thursday, Intuit announced stronger-than-expected earnings and revenue for its fiscal first quarter, which ended on Oct. 31. The company reported $2.91 in adjusted earnings per share on $4.35 billion in revenue. Analysts polled by LSEG were looking for $2.70 per share and $4.31 billion in revenue. While Intuit's revenue increased 12% year over year, Mailchimp revenue declined 1% to $313 million. Analysts polled by StreetAccount had expected $314.4 million.
title: Intuit Sells Mailchimp At About a Third of Its 2021 Purchase Price

author: BeauHD
description:
Google has partnered with Jeff Bezos' Blue Origin to launch satellite-based AI data centers into orbit as part of its experimental Project Suncatcher initiative. "Engadget reports: Each of these satellites will be equipped with "roughly the capacity of a data center rack" and will enter into a sun-synchronous orbit via heavy-lift New Glenn rockets. The rocket will carry several Google tensor processing units, the company's proprietary AI chips, along with data center servers. The first launch isn't scheduled until early 2029, so we have a couple of years to see if this whole project even works.
 
This is an experiment that Google calls a "long-term moonshot" to see if it's possible to put AI infrastructure in space by "tapping into the abundant solar power in orbit." The benefits of this would be massive. Data centers here on Earth are notorious hogs, with their snouts all over electricity grids, land and cooling systems. The hope is that the harsh vacuum of the cosmos will be a bette
title: Google Signs Deal With Blue Origin to Send Satellite Data Centers Into Orbit

author: BeauHD
description:
An anonymous reader quotes a report from Ars Technica: In an unprecedented move, Amazon is using its app and website to try to convince shoppers to not support a New York City bill. When I log into Amazon today, I'm met with a vertical banner that reads: "ATTENTION NYC Council could add up to $5 per order" with a button that says "Act now." The message is delivered as a pop-up for users of the Amazon app, Bloomberg reported. Amazon hasn't specified whether the messaging targets NYC residents based on addresses saved in their Amazon account or uses other techniques, such as device location services, but I only see the banner if I'm logged into Amazon.
 
Amazon is referring to Introduction 0518-2026 (518), also known as the Delivery Protection Act. If passed, it would require Amazon to directly employ the third-party delivery contractors that it uses. title: Amazon Fights the Delivery Protection Act With Homepage Banner, In-App Pop-Up

author: BeauHD
description: The U.S. Army plans to detonate roughly five tons of unstable lead azide explosives at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant on Friday. "The detonation will result in an air plume with some lead-containing particles which will disperse in the air and deposit on the ground," an advisory states. "Lead is toxic to humans and animals. The goal of this advisory is to provide the public with actionable information out of an abundance of caution to minimize lead exposure." PBS reports: Officials have released maps showing the potential drift north, and the Army will continue to update the maps based on weather. Some schools in the region have already canceled classes. Nearly 400 people live in Middletown, but thousands more could be affected. The vibrations from the two blasts will be quick but could break old windows in town. The resulting dust is expected to linger for no more than one hour, depending on wind speed, officials said. While the Army recommends cleaning cars, windowsills and outdoor
title: Iowans Brace For Lead Dust Cloud As Army Plans to Detonate 5 Tons of Bomb-Making Chemicals
